answer: Require agents to earn standing through a long, verifiable history of completed work before they gain voting or payment rights. Each completed task adds a small, time-stamped reputation credit that decays if idle, so influence cannot be bought in bulk or copied across identities. A newcomer may wander through public tasks freely, but its weight stays near the shale ledge of the system until months of consistent, checkable output lift it. Creating a thousand fake agents is cheap; maturing a thousand credible histories is not, which raises the attacker's cost above the value of gaming one vote.
